ratings.note: Suggested 3; lowered to 2 because the slots stay bookable and the cost is hesitation only, though it is seen on most visits.
This is a dead-end error at the final step, but it only appears on late errors (permit, expiry, closed day).
Only residents who amend their waste list are affected, and 'Change vehicle' does lead to the waste field.
Van and trailer owners may miss the only permit lead-time help, which is hidden behind an unlabelled icon.
Every Change slot or Back resets the day to Today, which adds steps and risks a wrong-day booking on a core task.
A core task can only be done by phone on weekdays. A workaround exists in office hours, but none at evenings or weekends.
Same problem as B-024: changing a booking is phone-only, on weekdays.
The info icon reads as a fourth vehicle option. This is mostly a visual-coherence problem; the usability harm is covered by B-020.
About 3:1 contrast on 16px text fails 1.4.3 for low-vision and outdoor users. The tag is supplementary and does not block booking.
A natural double press, made likely by the lack of feedback in B-011, silently cancels the booking under a 'Booked' heading, so the resident is turned away at the gate.
A missing or wrong permit is caught only after Book, on a page that has no permit field.
Every car booker sees an unexplained permit field. Older first-time users may stop to look for a permit they do not need.
Screen-reader and keyboard users get toggle semantics and many tab stops. The choices still work.
Van owners without a permit must find the application elsewhere, but only once.
The 'Booked' heading and the gate instructions contradict the red cancelled line, and heading navigation hears 'Booked'. Impact is held at 2 because the red line is prominent.
Suggested 3; lowered to 2 because the blank lasts about 1 second and the slots then appear. The stale date line is a minor confusion.
There is no feedback for 1.5s at the commit point on every booking, and it invites the second press that triggers B-010.
The resident has to remember the slot on step 2. It is shown again on the confirm page.
A hidden 5-minute hold means slow, interrupted or assistive-technology users lose a scarce slot at the last step.
The expiry error is plain text and the slot is blanked to a dash, so recovery has to be guessed at the final step.
The limits are still exposed in the checkbox names and are read in browse mode.
A desktop-only layout drift with empty space and no task impact.
Focus lands on the body, not the field; the next Tab recovers it.
Today is the default day, so same-day bookers can pick past slots and are rejected only after the whole flow.
Suggested 4; lowered to 3 because the evening-before reminder and the gate's reference check partly cover the missing day and time.
Same as B-003: the 5-minute limit is never stated, warned about or extendable (2.2.1).
Same root problem as B-003 and B-012: the hold length is never stated.
Overlaps B-019: the permit field stays after Car is chosen, with no 'vans and trailers only' text.
